1:א: (1) A place that has three partitions — meaning such as a mavo open on the fourth side, or a courtyard where one of its walls was breached and between them is open to karmelit or reshus ha-rabbim:
1:ב: (2) The Sages forbade moving objects in it — within four amot; and the reason they forbade it is that since the fourth side is fully open it somewhat resembles reshus ha-rabbim, and if we permit this they will come to move objects also in reshus ha-rabbim; and see Biur Halacha:
1:ג: (3) Some correction on the fourth side — meaning as explained below in seif 2 and seif 3, each according to its law:
2:א: (4) That was breached — meaning to a forbidden place for it:
2:ג: (6) Up to ten amot — and "up to" includes it; for although generally we hold that if a wall was breached ten amot the breach is considered an opening, here since the entire wall is missing we cannot consider this place an opening:
2:ד: (7) In one place — meaning at the top of the wall:
2:ה: (8) One tefach from here, etc. — not specifically one tefach but two mashehuyin suffice, as likewise for placing pasin l'chatchila, and as Beit Yosef wrote; and see Biur Halacha:
2:ו: (9) At a height of ten tefachim — and it need not be equal in height to the other walls; however below this it has no name of partition at all:
2:ז: (10) Since it is fully — this "fully" is not precise, for even if two or three tefachim remained from the wall, any minority relative to the breach requires correction; rather it comes to exclude where standing is greater, for there we hold the majority is as the whole and it is as closed, and even though it does not hold four tefachim, any slight amount more than the breach suffices:
2:ח: (11) Until there remains in it less than three — meaning that one corrects the breach in part and only less than three remains, for then it is as lavud; and all the more if the breach was only less than three, for then no correction is needed for this reason:
2:ט: (12) Even if it is not fully — this wording is not precise, for even when standing is greater than the breach it is also forbidden, as if the entire wall were breached. And tzurat hapetach helps even when it is fully:
3:א: (13) They permitted by a lechi — and although in a courtyard we require specifically a pas four tefachim wide, here the Sages were lenient; and the reason is that the more something is made for dwelling and private uses, the more complete partitions are required; therefore courtyards, whose custom is that homeowners use them more for private uses and eating, require their partitions to be more complete so that there is reshut ha-yachid upon them, unlike mavo'ot where they do not use them for private uses; therefore a mavo suffices with a lechi; and see below siman 366 that this is specifically when its opening is not wider than ten amot, and further details see there:
3:ב: (14) Any amount — even less than a fingerbreadth (Acharonim):
3:ג: (15) At the opening of the mavo — see below siman 361:
3:ד: (16) Ten tefachim — spaced and not precise [Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger]; and ten tefachim help even for a mavo twenty amot high:
3:ה: (17) And even if he tied, etc. — and it deals with when they did not inform that they placed it for the sake of lechi; if so certainly it will go away and not stand there all day, therefore we require specifically tying; and some are stringent even when they informed, lest he forget and go away from there:
4:א: (18) If there is some wall, etc. — although it was not made for the sake of lechi, we hold that a lechi standing by itself is also valid, as below in seif 11 see there:
4:ב: (19) A width of one tefach — see Biur Halacha:
5:א: (20) A lechi that if wind blows, etc. — and the same when making tzurat hapetach, for it is not better than a partition that cannot stand in an ordinary wind, which is not a partition [Tosafot Shabbos and Shach]; and even if the wind does not knock it to the ground but only shakes it, as written siman 362 seif 1:
5:ב: (21) Is not considered a lechi — it appears to me that if the lechi below does not shake, such as if fixed with a nail or tied well to the wall, and for this reason it does not shake until along a height of ten tefachim, and only above it shakes by wind because of its great height — it is valid, for from what remains above there is still lechi measure:
6:א: (22) It is required that it not be — some say the reason is because the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it; and accordingly if the lechi were wider than three tefachim it is valid even if the lechi were distant three tefachim from the wall, for this is standing greater than the breach at its side, and in such a case we do not say the air comes and nullifies it; and some say that in every case the lechi must be within three tefachim of the wall, and one should be stringent:
6:ב: (23) The lechi — and when establishing tzurat hapetach for a mavo, the view of many poskim is that one need not be precise that it be within three tefachim of the wall, for tzurat hapetach is a complete partition; and some poskim hold there is no difference between tzurat hapetach and lechi for this matter, and in a time of need one may rely to be lenient. And if there are four tefachim between tzurat hapetach and the wall, the view of Chayei Adam is that one must place a lechi next to the wall; and for my part it requires further study also in this, as I clarified in Biur Halacha; and l'chatchila it is certainly proper to be concerned to be stringent even when distant three tefachim from the wall:
7:א: (24) A lechi — even fragments, etc. — meaning attached, provided it can stand in an ordinary wind [Levush]. And to exclude a korah, for we require specifically that it be strong enough to receive a brick, as below in seif 17:
7:ב: (25) Are valid for it — and the same for stones protruding from the wall and separated from one another less than three tefachim — they are an actual lechi, provided that between all of them there is a height of ten tefachim:
7:ג: (26) And therefore they make a lechi, etc. — for it is no worse than fragments of fragments, which are permitted for lechi; and the same for tzurat hapetach, for we require that lechayim be made on this side and that side; if he fears the wind will knock them down, it is permitted to make them by plaster smeared on the wall on this side and that side, and the reed above should be aligned upon them; and nevertheless we require that there be some substance at least like a thread; but appearance of plaster alone, or a mark in lime called krayid, or another color — does not help [Taz and Shach]:
7:ד: (27) That it not be erased more, etc. — meaning by dogs and pigs that are accustomed to rub against walls and erase from the walls the plaster smear near the ground; then it no longer helps, neither for lechi nor for tzurat hapetach:
7:ה: (28) More than three toward the ground — this wording is not precise, for even if only three were erased precisely, it is also nullified from being a lechi, as below in seif 10:
8:א: (29) A lechi that one made, etc. — in the Gemara it states that one may make a lechi from asherah wood, and it implies even l'chatchila. And one should not question: although for lechi, since it does not require measure, cut down its measure does not apply, as below — nevertheless it is forbidden in benefit; one may say that since the lechi is only for the sake of partition and one does not use anything in it itself, benefit from what one benefits through it for permitting carrying is not considered benefit [Beit Meir see there]:
8:ב: (30) Valid — the reason is that since a lechi does not require measure and any amount suffices, as above in seif 3, even from asherah wood it helps, although asherah wood stands for burning and is as if burned, and cut down its measure — nevertheless it does not require measure; and although here it still requires at least height measure of ten tefachim, since one can make it a very thin line of any amount, the Sages were not stringent about such a small measure; and they also answered in this that for lechi, even if the wood were burned to ash and kneaded with ash and glued to the wall, it is also considered a lechi, provided it is not removable by wind; therefore it is not disqualified because it stands for burning:
9:א: (31) And it is not visible to those standing outside — such as if he placed the lechi with its width along the length of the mavo and did not draw the end of its width slightly outward, but aligned its outer end with the thickness of the mavo wall, and it is like one who adds to the wall thickness and is not visible from outside as a lechi; but its inner end is visible to those standing inside, as in the source a diagram appears:
9:ב: (32) Opposite the hollow of the mavo — such as if he placed the entire lechi outside the mavo and its inner end stands at the wall thickness, but he did not place it flush with the edge of the wall thickness on the inner side of the mavo, for then it would not appear as a lechi but as adding to the wall even for those standing in reshus ha-rabbim; rather they distanced it from the corner of the inner wall thickness and placed it at the edge of the thickness of the rear side of the mavo, so that by this it is recognizable to those standing outside in reshus ha-rabbim opposite the hollow of the mavo that it is a lechi, as in the source a diagram appears:
9:ג: (33) For those standing inside — meaning for those standing inside the mavo the lechi is not visible, for it is not made on the inside:
10:א: (34) If he distanced it from the wall three — although it was already taught in seif 6, it repeated it to inform us that it is for invalidation:
10:ב: (35) Or if he raised it from the ground three — meaning even though the lechi has ten tefachim; and the reason is that it is not better than a partition removed three tefachim from the ground, which is invalid because it is a partition under which kids break through, which is not called a partition:
10:ג: (36) Valid — because of lavud, and it is as if this empty space were filled:
11:א: (37) That happened to be there by itself — such as if a projection came out from the mavo wall at its top in the measure of a length ten tefachim high, or it was placed there for some purpose, and even if they did not fix it — it itself has always been there — it is also valid, for lechi is because of partition, and a partition standing by itself is valid:
11:ב: (38) Such as if there was another lechi there, etc. — for it is as if he said on this I rely and not on this, and this one is as if rejected from the category of lechi [Or Zarua]:
11:ג: (39) As if they relied on it — meaning although they did not rely on it explicitly; however if they did not rely on it explicitly, such as if they did not carry on the past Shabbat through this lechi and there was no other lechi there, it does not help for the coming Shabbat until they rely on it explicitly from erev Shabbat:
12:א: (40) A lechi standing, etc. — the measure of his words is thus: for that which is written in seif 11 that a lechi standing by itself and they relied on it helps — specifically if the lechi does not protrude into the width of the mavo four amot; but if it protrudes and extends from the house wall into the width of the mavo four amot, then it leaves the category of lechi [because it has the qualifying measure of mavo length, which is four amot, as below in siman 366], and there it is a mavo wall upon it, and another lechi is required at the mavo opening to permit it — unless the mavo does not hold its width except eight amot, for then it is permitted without another lechi, for it is standing as breached and the mavo is considered closed on all sides, as likewise in siman 362 seif 9:
12:ב: (41) By itself — for if he placed it for the sake of lechi, even four amot wide, it is a lechi, as written in the gloss:
12:ג: (42) Four amot — for four amot is the measure of a mavo wall, and there is no recognition at all that it is a lechi; but up to four amot we can count it as a lechi, and this is when they relied on it from erev Shabbat, as likewise in seif 11:
12:ד: (43) Even four amot wide — and the same for more than this; and the reason is that because he increased at the mavo opening in its closing, it is no worse than an ordinary lechi [Rashi]:
13:א: (44) One who extends along its side, etc. — along the length of the mavo:
13:ב: (45) That the end of the lechi does not cover, etc. — rather it is shorter than it and extends beyond toward the rear of the mavo, as we illustrated above in seif 9 in Mishna Berurah:
13:ג: (46) Up to its inner end — meaning that through the lechi it is permitted to use the entire mavo up to the inner end of the lechi and no more; for although we hold in siman 365 seif 4 that between lechayim it is permitted to use, here it is different, for the other side is shorter than this, for there is no side opposite the lechi:
13:ד: (47) Four amot — it is judged as a mavo — for since it is four amot, which is generally the measure of mavo length, it leaves the category of lechi and is counted as a mavo wall; and likewise a mavo where one made along the length of the mavo inward many small lechayim arranged less than three tefachim from one another along four amot — the mavo is not permitted by this, for since they are less than three tefachim from one another, they are all considered as one lechi holding four amot in its width, and it leaves the category of lechi and is counted as a wall, and there is no lechi for this mavo. And nevertheless, if the first lechi standing at the end of the mavo does not stand flush with the end of the mavo but extends somewhat from the mavo inward, it is judged as lechi since it is visible from outside:
13:ה: (48) And it is forbidden to use — for this is forbidden even if it was placed for the sake of lechi, and it is not similar to what was stated above in seif 12, where they permit there when placed for lechi, for there he placed the projection across the width of the mavo and thereby its opening was closed, and therefore it is no worse than a lechi; unlike here, where he placed it along its length and it appears as adding further to the wall:
14:א: (49) By a korah — so that through it there will be recognition that they should not come to confuse and carry in a full reshus ha-rabbim, and also that they should not come to carry from it outward:
14:ב: (50) On the head of the mavo — meaning at the end of the mavo; and if he placed it in the middle of the mavo, see below in seif 362:
14:ג: (51) But if he drove, etc. — meaning that he inserted two pegs into the two walls on this side and that toward reshus ha-rabbim; and what is written "even close to it" means the pegs were very short, and automatically when he placed the korah on them it was close to the walls without any gap between them — nevertheless it is invalid; and the reason is that for a korah on walls we require that it not appear that it came to qualify the mavo, but only when it is within the hollow of the mavo, for it is not the way of any ceiling or korah to place it except on the walls and not from outside; and specifically for korah, but for lechi we do not require within the hollow of the mavo, but even outside the hollow of the mavo, and like that case of seif 13 above; and the reason of the matter is that a lechi, even standing outside, is recognizable that it came to qualify the mavo, unlike a korah, as explained:
14:ד: (52) Invalid — and if he drove two pegs into the ground close to the mavo walls on this side and that from outside and placed the korah on them, it is valid because of lechi [Or Zarua and R' Akiva Eiger and Shach]:
15:א: (53) But if not, etc. — like one who places a korah from wall to wall to strengthen the walls, and all similar cases:
15:ב: (54) Even if they relied on it, etc. — and although for lechi we hold in seif 12 that if they relied on it from erev Shabbat it helps even when standing by itself — there it is different, for lechi is because of partition, and a partition standing by itself is also a partition; but a korah is because of recognition, and when it was not placed for that purpose there is no recognition; and see Peri Megadim who sides that even if the korah were four tefachim wide it also does not help; and see Biur Halacha:
16:א: (55) Requires measure — as below in seif 17:
16:ב: (56) And therefore, etc. — and the same for anything that requires measure, such as what was mentioned above in seif 2, a pas of four tefachim on one side, or one tefach from here and one tefach from here:
16:ג: (57) From asherah wood — that a Jew worked it so it has no nullification, or even of a gentile and a Jew cut it [for if a gentile cut it, behold it was nullified automatically, as stated in Yoreh De'ah siman 146 seif 6], and the Jew took it for his benefit, for by this gentile property becomes Israel property that has no nullification; therefore we say cut down its measure applies to it; but if the Jew did not take it for his benefit, it is gentile property of a gentile that has nullification, and since it has nullification we do not say cut down its measure, even before it was nullified:
17:א: (58) One tefach wide — and although it requires measure to receive upon it a brick that is one tefach and a half wide, one can join a quarter tefach from it in mortar here and a quarter tefach from it there [Gemara]:
17:ב: (59) To receive a brick, etc. — meaning bricks, each of which holds in its length three tefachim and in its width one tefach and a half, lying upon it along its entire length as the measure of the width of that mavo's opening [and nevertheless, if the mavo opening was ten amot wide, it need not be fit to receive bricks along its entire length; rather it suffices if it can receive bricks along a length of nine amot and two mashehuyin, which are eighteen bricks in their length, for a korah of nine amot and two mashehuyin permits a mavo of width ten amot by the law of lavud — meaning that it should not reach less than three tefachim to this wall and less than three tefachim to that wall, as below in siman 361]; and the reason it must be fit to receive bricks is that otherwise there would not be so much recognition that people of reshus ha-rabbim would think they placed it there temporarily; but when it is healthy and strong to receive such building, it is recognizable to all that building placement was intended for this purpose:
18:א: (60) That are not one tefach wide, etc. — for otherwise those placing them would themselves have the status of korah upon them, and also their length would not be three so that the korah would be lavud to the wall, as all explained in siman 365:
18:ב: (61) And to support half a brick — and as explained in seif 17:
18:ג: (62) Rather only to support it — for one does not place bricks upon it; and for korah we require permanence so that there be excellent recognition, but the recognition does not depend on those placing it [Rashi]; and l'chatchila it is proper to be stringent like the first view:
19:_: (63) If the korah was round, etc. — and although now when it is round it cannot receive a brick upon it, nevertheless it is valid, for we consider it as if it were divided in two [Rashi]:
20:א: (64) Inclines outside the mavo, etc. — for all these matters disqualify a korah:
20:ב: (65) We view whatever if one removed, etc. — and the reason is that we say lavud:
20:ג: (66) And if not — it is invalid; meaning specifically in this manner, where part of the bent korah is outside the qualifying measure of the mavo; but if it is entirely within the mavo as required, even if the bend is much more than three tefachim, it is valid, for we say we view it as if it were straight [thus it is evident from Rambam's conclusion in chapter 17 law 26 see there, and likewise from other Rishonim; however in Sefer Gaon Yaakov and in Chiddushei Even HaEzer they question this, see there]:
21:א: (67) And it does not touch, etc. — and even if distant from the two walls in such a manner, such as if he drove a tree in the middle of the mavo and placed a korah on it, we say lavud from two directions:
21:ב: (68) Invalid — rather he must bring another korah, or see to fill that gap with a piece of korah:
22:א: (69) Meaning one tefach — meaning that together they should be one tefach wide:
22:ב: (70) And there are not three tefachim between them — we consider them as if adjacent to one another because of lavud:
22:ג: (71) And some say, etc. — they hold that lavud does not apply here to permit, for we require that the korah be fit to receive a brick in its width, and when they are far apart they cannot receive a brick upon them:
22:ד: (72) Within one tefach — for a brick in its width holds one tefach and a half, and there must be at least a quarter tefach leaning from it upon this korah and a quarter upon the other; if so, the gap between them will not remain except the measure of one tefach and no more:
23:א: (73) If it was, etc. — here he comes to add a leniency on the previous seif, that even if the two korot that cannot each receive a brick were not standing level but one was higher than its fellow up to three tefachim, it is also valid, for we say we view, etc.:
23:ב: (74) And the lower one, etc. — meaning, or the lower one [Rashi]:
23:ג: (75) Provided, etc. — twenty; for if it is above twenty, then even if the lower one is adjacent to it within three tefachim, we do not say as if it were below twenty, since now it stands in an invalid place; and likewise if the lower one is below ten and the upper is adjacent within three tefachim, we do not say we view the lower as if standing level with the upper, since now it has no korah qualification:
23:ד: (76) With intent — meaning aligned; and this is that even if we consider that this one already descended somewhat and the lower one ascended somewhat until they became opposite one another level, they would then be distant only less than three tefachim, for then lavud applies, as likewise in the previous seif in the first view:
23:ה: (77) And some disqualify — because they hold we do not say we view the upper, etc.; and although below in the laws of sukkah in siman 631 the Mechaber ruled plainly in seif 5 that if the s'chach is mixed and one above and one below, if there are not three tefachim between them we say lavud — here it is different, for we require that they be fit to receive a brick, and with one above and one below they are not fit to receive a brick [Or Zarua]; and this is that even if they are one tefach higher than one another it also does not help; and even if standing exactly level, this view holds like the second view above, that we require specifically that they be adjacent to one another, not more than one tefach; and Avraham Rabba wrote one should be stringent like this view:
24:א: (78) A mat — that he wished to strengthen the permission and spread a mat over it, and also tied it to the wall so wind would not move it, so that there would also be a partition name upon it:
24:ב: (79) Invalid — even if the mat itself is ten high:
24:ג: (80) And it is not visible — if so there is no recognition here:
24:ד: (81) A wide korah — meaning that it is ten tefachim wide; and one might have thought that since it is so wide, a partition name is upon it and not a korah name, and a partition is not valid when it is high from the ground greatly, like a mat — it informs us that it is valid, for because of its greatness the korah name was not nullified from it; and a mat is different, for it covered the korah and it is not recognizable:
24:ה: (82) And extends somewhat below ten — several Acharonim questioned his words, for it appears from his wording that he comes to inform us that even part of the wide korah enters within the lower ten tefachim of the mavo, it is also valid, for we say we view this portion as if it were not there and the korah stands only above ten, as the korah qualification explained in siman 366; but in truth this is not so, for if part of the korah width entered within the airspace of the lower ten, it is invalid, for we require that the hollow of the mavo up to the korah be precisely ten tefachim:
25:א: (83) Bent on two, etc. — meaning that the pegs stood on the two sides on a slope and their heads protrude above the height of the walls:
25:ב: (84) And he placed the korah on them — meaning, and here there are two deficiencies: first, the korah is not placed on the wall itself but only in the air above on the pegs; second, the korah is shorter than the area between the two walls:
25:ג: (85) And the pegs are not one tefach — for if the pegs were one tefach wide, we would not care that the korah itself is short, for the pegs themselves are counted as korah:
25:ד: (86) Valid, etc. — for in that the pegs are not higher than the mavo walls by three tefachim, we say throw it down, meaning as if the korah were knocked down and lowered to the walls; and even though it is still short, since the inclination of the pegs is not three, and therefore the korah is not distant three tefachim from the walls, we say lavud:
25:ה: (87) Invalid — for in the measure of three we do not say throw down for korah, nor lavud:
26:א: (88) When it is not low — meaning that if the ground in the mavo is not low from inside opposite the walls by the measure of ten tefachim, it is considered as if the mavo has no partitions, for there is no partition less than ten:
26:ב: (89) Spaced — and in the latter clause precise; for we go stringently everywhere for this matter. And the measure of spaced over precise is half a fingerbreadth per amah:
26:ג: (90) More than ten — for if it is more than ten it has no name of opening, and lechi and korah do not help for this:
26:ד: (91) Precise — meaning that for each amah its six tefachim are measured precise; and likewise in the latter clause for mavo length, for we require four amot spaced, it is likewise that its tefachim are measured spaced; if so, two fingerbreadths are added to the four amot, as explained:
26:ה: (92) Its length four amot, etc. — for in less than this measure it is not considered a mavo but as a courtyard:
26:ו: (93) Only by tzurat hapetach — meaning that even if it was low less than ten tefachim, tzurat hapetach also helps; and likewise if the width is ten amot, or if its length was not four amot; but many Acharonim agreed with the ruling that if the hollow of the mavo was low less than ten tefachim, tzurat hapetach does not help, for even a partition does not help when it is not ten high, and all the more so mere tzurat hapetach. However, if the hollow of the mavo was ten tefachim high and only at the mavo opening it was low less than ten, in this tzurat hapetach helps, provided it was made as required — meaning the reeds were ten tefachim high [Gra]. And know further that if its length was not four amot, the view of several poskim is that its law is like a courtyard, and therefore it is also permitted by a pas of four on one side, or two pasin of mashehuyin on two sides; and likewise the Mechaber himself below in seif 362; and the Mechaber who wrote "only by tzurat hapetach" is not precise:
26:ז: (94) In the height of its hollow, etc. — but if the height of the hollow of the mavo up to the korah is only twenty precise, even though the korah is above twenty, it is valid:
26:ח: (95) Is not permitted by korah — for korah is because of recognition, and above twenty there is no recognition, for the eye does not rule over it; but a lechi, which is close to the ground and suffices at height nineteen — what harm is there if it is very high?:
26:ט: (96) To reduce it from twenty — and the same, he can lower the korah itself and place it within the hollow of the mavo on pegs protruding from the walls below twenty:
26:י: (97) In a structure one tefach wide — and the same for earth of this measure; and one must beware when trodden by feet that it not diminish from the measure in its width; and the same regarding its height, that it not diminish and become more than twenty:
26:כ: (98) In the width of the korah — for its measure is one tefach, as in seif 17; and the reason one tefach width helps is that we hold it is permitted to use beneath the korah, and one standing in that place can see the korah, for at that place it is not higher than twenty, and there is recognition because of this:
26:ל: (99) Must hollow four amot — and that which above one tefach suffices is different here, for in less than ten tefachim it is not called a side at all, and one must make it a side; therefore specifically the measure along the mavo length, which is four amot, is required, as at the beginning of this seif; but there it is called a side, only that it is higher than twenty amot, and therefore one tefach suffices as the measure of wall width (Rashi):
26:מ: (100) Into the mavo — and if he hollowed less than this, he requires specifically a pas of four, or two pasin of two mashehuyin, as the law of a courtyard, as explained at the end of the word "only":
26:נ: (101) Across its entire width — for if a gap remains between the hollowing and the walls, the walls cannot join to it, and it is as if there are no walls for the mavo. However, if the gap between the hollowing and the wall is only less than three tefachim, some say it helps [Peri Megadim]:
26:ס: (102) Two courtyards — the reason for this is that what they permitted in a mavo by lechi and korah is because it has many residents and they do not use it so much for privacy; therefore such a correction suffices; unlike a courtyard, where there are not so many residents, they use it more for privacy, therefore stricter qualification is required — two pasin or a pas of four; and the same for a mavo that does not have two courtyards open into it — few residents and they do private uses in it, therefore lechi and korah do not suffice:
26:ע: (103) And some disagree — for since they can join through the openings, they are considered as one courtyard; and the same for houses open to one another; and Acharonim wrote that since it is a rabbinic matter, we follow the lenient view:
26:פ: (104) And eats in his house — to exclude if his manner of eating is in his father's house:
26:צ: (105) That its length, etc. — for such is the way of a mavo to be:
26:ק: (106) More than its width — even any amount [and its length is called the way of its entry into the mavo, and what is not the way of entry is called width]; for if its length equals its width, it is as a courtyard, as below:
26:ר: (107) One of these — refers to all explained here from "a mavo is not permitted," etc.; and the same law when the mavo length was not four amot:
26:ש: (108) Is not permitted, etc. — for its law is like a courtyard, and therefore for this a pas of four tefachim, etc. is required, as above in seif 2:
26:ת: (109) Or tzurat hapetach — and this helps even when the width is ten, as above in seif 2:
26:23: (110) All mavo'ot, etc. — whether closed on one side, whether open on both sides, whether wide up to ten amot, whether more than ten amot:
26:24: (111) For all our mavo'ot, etc. — this is because in our mavo'ot there are no houses and courtyards open into them, and therefore they are not permitted by lechi and korah as the mavo permission law; and although in a courtyard two lechayim on two sides suffice without tzurat hapetach, nevertheless because sometimes the mavo is open on both sides, then certainly one must be stringent that it requires tzurat hapetach even without houses and courtyards open into it, because its head is open to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelit, or because sometimes it is wider than ten, for in this even in a courtyard tzurat hapetach is required by law, as in seif 2; therefore the practice was always to make tzurat hapetach. And behold, on the other side of a mavo, if the width is not more than ten amot, there are views among Acharonim — the view of many of them is that there in any case two lechayim on two sides suffice and tzurat hapetach is not required; their reason is that either way, if its law is like an open mavo, we also hold below in siman 364 that tzurat hapetach is not required except on one side, and on the other side one lechi or korah suffices; and if its law is like a courtyard, as explained, behold in any case two lechayim suffice; and some Acharonim side that from the practice one should make tzurat hapetach on every side. And certainly l'chatchila one must be careful in this; but in a place of need, such as if the rope over the lechayim broke on Shabbat or any similar case, it appears one may rely on them to be lenient where the width is not more than ten amot, even if it is fully breached. And behold, in our mavo'ot mentioned above that have no houses and courtyards open into them, if it is a crooked mavo, there are views among Acharonim whether correction is required in its bend as explained below in siman 364 seif 3; some say that since from the outset its law is like a courtyard, no correction is needed there, and what they do at its two heads suffices; and some are stringent in this, and the practice is to be lenient. And know further that what is explained that in our towns tzurat hapetach is required — this is in towns not surrounded by a wall, or surrounded by a wall and the wall was breached to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelit more than ten amot; but when surrounded by a wall and the wall was not breached, only that one must correct and divide between where Jews live and where gentiles live so they should not forbid Jews to carry — there one need not make tzurat hapetach, but a pas four tefachim wide or two pasin of mashehuyin suffices when breached there fully and the place is not wider than ten amot where one wishes to make the correction (even if the mavo in the middle is wider than ten amot), for this city has complete courtyard law. And when no correction was made between Jew and gentile, the law here is also like a courtyard, that it is permitted to carry vessels that rested within it, but not to a house and not from house to courtyard:
26:25: (112) Beneath the rope, etc. — and since the reeds below are ten tefachim high, no further reeds are needed above to tie the rope on them; rather he can tie the rope opposite them even on a roof above this and that, as we hold above at the end of siman 362 that the upper reed need not touch the lower reeds. Also that which is explained above at the end of siman 362, that one should not tie the upper reed or rope from the side of the reeds but only above upon them — here, when tying the rope above on the roof on some reed, it is not relevant to be precise about the manner of tying whether on top or from the side, provided the lower reeds are aligned beneath the rope. If there is a roof interrupting between the height of the rope and the lower reeds, it is not tzurat hapetach in this, since the roof interrupts between the rope and the reeds; and one does not make tzurat hapetach in such a matter, but must open a large hole in the roof above opposite the reeds so the reeds are aligned beneath the rope without interruption:
26:26: (113) Two reeds — on the ground, but the mavo walls are not counted in place of the reeds. And if there is a protruding pillar in the wall, it is judged as a reed if they relied on it from erev Shabbat, for it is no worse than lechi in seif 11. And the same when projections come out from the wall, less and less than three tefachim up to less than three tefachim near the ground — one may rely on them from erev Shabbat for reeds of tzurat hapetach, provided they are exposed above beneath the rope; and some are stringent with such projections that are not made in the manner of doorposts of an opening, and it is not considered an opening. If one places the reeds inside the house or inside the fence surrounding it on four sides, it is nothing; and even if he placed one reed there, it also does not help:
26:27: (114) Aligned beneath the rope — and if something protrudes from the side, it is invalid:
26:28: (115) In the category of tzurat hapetach — meaning, and it helps even when more than ten amot:
27:_: (116) Whose length is more than its width — even any amount [Gemara]; and its length is called the way of entry. And it is not judged as a courtyard unless its length and width are equal, or its width exceeds its length [Magen Avraham]:
28:_: (117) That does not have three tefachim in its width — and commentators wrote that if its opening does not have width of three, no correction is required even if inside it is very wide; and likewise for the view that holds we require specifically width of four — it deals when there was width of four in all the walls, but where it narrows near its opening, no correction is required even if inside is very wide. And behold from the Mechaber it appears he holds primarily like the first view, that where it is three wide correction is required; and see Darkhei Moshe who disagrees, and his view is that we can be lenient like the other view, see there; and in my humble opinion it appears that even if we are stringent like the first view, that where it is three wide correction is required — this is specifically where inside it was at least four wide but narrows at its opening as explained; but where throughout it is not four wide, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:א: (118) Ends at the sea — meaning that the mavo had two sides from houses and courtyards, and its two heads east and west — one ended at the sea and one ended at a public garbage heap ten tefachim high from the ground; therefore it needs nothing, for the sea is also considered a partition ten tefachim deep at its edge, and water does not nullify the partition, as written siman 356; and Magen Avraham wrote that here it deals with a place where ships do not pass there to the port, for otherwise many come and nullify the partition; but several Acharonim disagree on this and hold that even when ships pass there, the partition at the sea edge is not nullified thereby. [However, when one head of the mavo ends at a river and there is a bridge over it where many walk to the other side, it appears from several Acharonim that through the bridge the partition is nullified and tzurat hapetach must be made at the place of the bridge.] And all this is specifically when the sea or river edge was ten tefachim deep; but if the sea and river edge slopes and continues, if along the slope four amot it is still not ten tefachim high, it is not a partition, for it is like level ground. And all this when the river is immediately adjacent to the head of the mavo; but if it is distant from the houses more than ten amot, correction is required, for that place is breached; and if it freezes in winter months, then the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry; and some Acharonim hold the partition is not nullified by freezing. And if the river edge is high and ten tefachim collect within four amot up to the place of freezing, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:ב: (119) Is not made to be cleared — for all day they throw their refuse and manure there and its height will not diminish; but an individual's garbage heap, although now it is ten tefachim high, tomorrow it will be cleaned and its height will be lacking; and if we permit now to carry, they will also carry later when its height is lacking:
29:ג: (120) And we are not concerned, etc. — meaning also we are not concerned lest the partition on the sea side be ruined and it be found that the mavo has no fourth partition:
29:ד: (121) The sea rises as a sandbar — for such is the way of the sea, that it raises sand and stones at its edge and shortens and becomes land the width of a parasang, and the partitions are nullified and they also carry in mavo'ot as at first [and all this when there is no slope except at the place of the water alone; but if on its edge there is a slope that collects ten tefachim within four amot, this is considered a partition in every regard]; and Acharonim agreed to be stringent like this view, and specifically for seas; but for rivers we are not concerned that a sandbar will rise, and we consider the river edge a partition when it has ten tefachim height [however rivers whose way is to dry in summer, and when they dry their slope does not have ten tefachim high within four amot — one should forbid without correction even when not yet dry, for we are concerned it will dry without awareness]. And in any case we require that the river be immediately adjacent to the head of the mavo; but if it is distant from the houses more than ten amot, correction is required, for that place is breached; and if rivers freeze in winter months, then the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry; and some Acharonim hold the partition is not nullified by freezing. And if the river edge is high and ten tefachim collect within four amot up to the place of freezing, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:ה: (122) And there is no partition here — and therefore correction is required like any mavo breached on the fourth side, by tzurat hapetach or lechi or korah. A city surrounded by a ditch ten tefachim deep and four tefachim wide is as surrounded by a wall, and no correction is required; and if there is a bridge over the ditch where they walk to the city's mavo'ot, it was explained above that correction must be made there:
30:א: (123) That one side is long — and its wall extends to reshus ha-rabbim more than the other wall:
30:ב: (124) Even if the side, etc. — four amot — and the same even if less than this, he places only opposite the short side specifically and not diagonally; and the reason is that korah is made for recognition so they should not come to confuse with reshus ha-rabbim; and diagonally there is no recognition — meaning, if he places it diagonally and uses on the long side opposite the long, where there is no side opposite it, the viewer will say it is permitted to use reshus ha-rabbim, because that excess does not appear to be from the mavo; and this is the reason he later permitted in Shulchan Aruch to place the korah inside the mavo diagonally, for there they will not come through this to err and permit use in reshus ha-rabbim:
30:ג: (125) He should make tzurat hapetach there diagonally — and use on the short opposite the short and on the long opposite the long; and the reason is that tzurat hapetach is like a complete partition, and a complete partition certainly helps even diagonally, and even if the mavo opening width were more than ten amot, it is also permitted through tzurat hapetach, as at the beginning of siman 366; but if he places one lechi at the long side and one lechi at the short side, they do not help to use diagonally, and even if the diagonal were not more than ten amot, for although lechi is not only because of recognition but because of partition, nevertheless a lechi on the long side does not help to permit use next to it, since there is no partition opposite it, and it is not permitted to use except opposite the lechi standing on the short side, which permits only directly opposite it. However, this is specifically in a mavo permitted by one lechi; but in a courtyard requiring two pasin, or in our mavo'ot that have courtyard law, even up to the short place one is also not permitted to use, since we cannot join to it the other lechi that does not stand opposite it; therefore one must be careful where placing two lechayim to place them level opposite one another and not diagonally [Chayei Adam]; and tzurat hapetach helps even diagonally, as explained. Rashba's novellae wrote that tzurat hapetach helps even if one side exceeds its fellow by four amot and more, for it is like a complete partition:
30:ד: (126) He may place, etc. — see Taz who sides that specifically if diagonally it is not more than ten amot, for otherwise it is forbidden; and see Biur Halacha:
31:א: (127) Until they join together — meaning that they participate together; and the reason is that behold the way of mavo'ot is that after correcting them with lechi or korah, all residents of the mavo participate together [for when they do not participate they will be forbidden to take out from the courtyards to the mavo]; and since the custom is thus, the mavo residents are again forbidden to divide into halves and each make participation by himself, for these forbid those, because it is like a mavo where one of the courtyards forgot and did not participate, which forbids the whole:
31:ב: (128) And they did not make, etc. — for since they did not make a lechi and cannot carry in the mavo, they are not fit to participate together; therefore they cannot forbid the inner one, even if they have habitual passage upon it [Peri Megadim]:
31:ג: (129) From it outward — forbidden — for we consider as if the mavo began from the lechi inward:
31:ד: (130) But if they made in the middle, etc. — in this the domains are divided from one another, and it is as if there is a partition between them, and they cannot forbid one another; and specifically when they do not have habitual passage one upon the other, such as if they have another opening; but otherwise even a door does not help:
31:ה: (131) Two pasin — of mashehuyin, something from here and something from here; and even a courtyard can be divided in such a manner. A city surrounded by a wall and the gates are locked at night and one gate is not locked — nevertheless through that gate it is like lechi; through that opening one may not divide it in halves; but if a breach was made, its qualification was nullified [and see siman 365 seif 2 through which breach the qualification was nullified] of the city, and they can join half and leave half:
32:_: (132) And all this in a place, etc. — this "and all this" refers to where we qualified by placing a lechi in the middle of the mavo when they did not make a lechi at the head of the mavo; and it says that this is specifically when in this half of the mavo alone there is also mavo name, that it has all the conditions required for this [as Shulchan Aruch concludes and as written above in siman 366]; if not so, it has courtyard law and requires a mashehu pas, etc., as above in seif 2; and Shulchan Aruch does not refer to if they also made lechi outside and joined together, for for this one need not have all the details in that half of the mavo, for the entire mavo joins together for this [Peri Megadim]; and see there what he wrote further on this:
33:א: (133) That it is twenty amot wide — and it deals with when he does not wish to make tzurat hapetach at the mavo opening, for this helps even however wide the mavo is, as at the end of siman 366:
33:ב: (134) Four amot wide — and in less than this it does not help, even though each side is less than ten, for the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it; unlike when he makes it four amot wide as the measure along a mavo wall, as in siman 366 — air from here and there cannot nullify it, for air cannot nullify a mavo wall. And what is written "and he places it in the middle" means along the length of the mavo:
33:ג: (135) Since its length, etc. — and it is also required that the pas not be low less than ten tefachim, as the law of a mavo wall, as in siman 366:
33:ד: (136) At its head — meaning that it reaches from one mavo wall to the wall opposite it, to permit both sides; and the same, he can correct them by lechayim — lechi from here and lechi from here, or lechi on one and korah on one [meaning one head on the mavo wall and its other head on the pas], like other mavo'ot:
33:ה: (137) Placed on the pas, etc. — to exclude if the pas is low, even though the korah touches from this wall to the opposite wall, it does not help, for behold through the pas it is considered as two mavo'ot, for it is considered as a wall, and if so each mavo's korah is placed only on one wall:
33:ו: (138) Or within, etc. — for it is as lavud:
33:ז: (139) And every condition of a mavo — as explained above in siman 366; if not so, its law is like a courtyard, and korah does not help in it, but only two lechayim of mashehu on its two sides, as explained above in seif 2:
33:ח: (140) And what is from the pas, etc. — meaning, besides the korah correction made at the mavo opening, one must make another correction at the end of the pas length, as the law of a crooked mavo explained in siman 364 end of seif 3, even if there are not ten amot from the end of the pas length to the middle wall:
33:ט: (141) Bent in the middle and open — should read: bent in the middle and open:
33:י: (142) At their two heads to reshus ha-rabbim — and therefore one must make tzurat hapetach at the end of the pas length to the middle wall opposite it, and it is like one who made a pas along the entire mavo length:
33:כ: (143) For it does not have crooked mavo law, etc. — for although it is explained below in siman 364 regarding a crooked mavo made like a chet, that even if from the beginning of the bend to the middle wall is not ten amot, correction is still required there — there it is different, for it is actually crooked; but here one can say that through the pas they become as two mavo'ot completely divided to their ends; and although the pas does not reach the middle wall, nevertheless since from the end of the pas to the opposite wall is not more than ten amot, it is considered an opening and is like two mavo'ot completely divided, only that there is an opening from one to the other; unlike when more than ten amot, one cannot say it is like an opening, and therefore its law is like a crooked mavo; and for practical law Acharonim agreed the main view is like the first reasoning; and see Biur Halacha:
33:ל: (144) More than ten amot — as it should read:
34:א: (145) And he makes a pas three amot wide — for thereby standing becomes greater than the breach at its side and it is considered closed; and although generally we hold that breach like standing is also permitted, as explained in siman 362 seif 9 — here it is different, for it is also breached from the other side, and in such a case where they are equal we say the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it:
34:ב: (146) And an opening ten amot wide remains — and nevertheless lechi or korah is required to permit the mavo, for it is not better than other ordinary mavo'ot; and one places the korah only on the area of ten amot [and likewise when making lechi, he places it at the head of the ten amot], for from the pasin onward until the walls it is permitted otherwise because of standing greater than breach:
34:ג: (147) And likewise every similar case — meaning that he distances four amot from the wall and makes a pas of six amot [Rashi]:
34:ד: (148) And one must beware, etc. — but from the default we are not concerned lest they walk through the small one and leave the large one, for the presumption is that a person does not leave a large opening and enter through a small one:
34:ה: (149) That if he did so, etc. — meaning that thereby the opening status of the large one is nullified, and the lechi or korah corrected in it is nullified, and this mavo is found without correction:
34:ו: (150) For the small one — see Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger who wonders what helps in making tzurat hapetach for the small one after opening status was nullified from the large one; and the correct view is as written in Sefer Tiferet Shmuel that it is a scribal error and should read "for the large one," and now it is well explained that after tzurat hapetach was made, opening status was not nullified from it even if they do not walk through it:
35:_: (151) When complete it is considered — meaning, and therefore it is not relevant to say in this the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it:
36:א: (152) And a slope to reshus ha-rabbim — where the mavo ground was higher than reshus ha-rabbim ground and he had to slope at its opening toward reshus ha-rabbim:
36:ב: (153) Or level to reshus ha-rabbim, etc. — where reshus ha-rabbim was higher than mavo ground, and the mavo entry also from the opening inward was high like reshus ha-rabbim ground for the width of an amah or half an amah, and afterward it became a slope toward the middle side:
36:ג: (154) That raises ten, etc. — meaning that if the slope is four amot long, then the ground is already raised above ten tefachim and is like a partition; but if ten collect within five amot, it is as if it does not exist and is like other ground whose use is pleasant for walking:
36:ד: (155) And it requires no correction — for that height at the side of the opening is a partition, even though it slopes and continues; and this is what Rama concludes, "and with this mound," etc.:
36:ה: (156) And with this mound, etc. — and if the entire city is surrounded by a mound and afterward they built houses in it, it is forbidden, for it is not enclosed for dwelling, as written siman 358 seif 2; and see there seif 8, that even if he built partitions ten high on the mound it does not help; and if the mound was less than ten tefachim and he completed to ten tefachim, it helps, for this enclosure is enclosure for dwelling made after the city was built. Therefore one can correct even if the mound was around the entire city — meaning he diminishes from the mound in an area more than ten amot wide until it is not ten tefachim high, for then it is considered a breach, and afterward he completes this measure, and through this it helps, as above in siman 358 seif 2 see there:
36:ו: (157) Like a partition — and if around the city there is a ditch ten tefachim deep and four tefachim wide, which is like a partition, and the ditch was closed with earth and stones — if the closing does not rise more than ten amot, behold it is like an opening and does not forbid; but if it is more than ten amot, behold it is like a breach:
